question.problem:
Consider a curve $r(s)$ parametrized by its arc length $s.$ Find the radius of curvature of $r(s)$ at an arbitrary point knowing that its unit tangent vector $T(s)$ is given by

$$
T(s)=\frac{1}{2}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{8}),\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{8}),\,\sqrt{3}⟩.
$$

current_example.problem:
Consider a curve $\mathbf r(s)$ parametrized by its arc length $s.$ Find the radius of curvature of $\mathbf r(s)$ at an arbitrary point knowing that  its  unit tangent vector $\mathbf T(s)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}T(s) & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{3})\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{3})\,j\,.\end{aligned}
$$
current_example.worked_solution:
Since the curve $\mathbf{r}(s)$ and its unit tangent vector $\mathbf T(s)$ are both parametrized by arc length $s,$ we will use the following formula for the radius of curvature:

$$
R(s) = \dfrac{1}{\kappa(s)} = \dfrac{1}{\|\mathbf T'(s)\|}
$$

We differentiate $\mathbf T(s)$ with respect to $s$ and calculate its magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(s) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{3}))i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{3}))\,j \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{3})\,i-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{3})\,j \\ ‖{T}^{′}(s)‖ & =\sqrt{(-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{3}))^{2}+(-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{3}))^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{9}({cos}^{2}⁡(\frac{s}{3})+{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{s}{3}))} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the radius of curvature is

$$
R(s) = \dfrac{1}{\|\mathbf T'(s)\|} = \dfrac{1}{\:\dfrac{1}{3}\:} = 3\,.
$$
